title: Trump, Putin & Xi’s New Photo Op Looks Like This Classic ’90s Album: Here’s How the Internet Is Reacting
summary: No word yet on which fourth leader could round out the trio's inadvertent Weezer homage.
contentText:
Ever since its 1994 release, the album art for Weezer ‘s self-titled debut, commonly known as The Blue Album, has been meme fodder. Whenever a group of people stands before a blue background, observers note the resemblance to the famous record’s cover.

Related

Weezer’s Biggest Billboard Chart Hits: ‘Buddy Holly,’ ‘Beverly Hills’ & More

Now, three major world leaders have (almost certainly inadvertently) recreated the album cover. At the Thursday (Nov. 19) trilateral summit between the United States, Russia and China, respective leaders Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping posed for photos in front of a blue backdrop; naturally, the internet quickly took notice.

“The Orange Album” read one trending post on the Weezer subreddit, with comments including “geezer,” “My name is POTUS” and “Everything Won’t Be Alright in the End” (the latter two referring to Blue’s opening track, “My Name Is Jonas,” and the band’s 2014 album Everything Will Be Alright in the End ). Of the historically nonpartisan band, one commenter noted, “Low-key they should make a political album and have this as the cover.”

Another enterprising Redditor posted “An Equation for the Nerds” presenting the addition of a picture of the power-pop band Tally Hall in neckties and the Blue artwork presented as equaling the photo of the three politicians. Other comments on Reddit posts of the image: “Album cover for the ‘Everybody Wants to Rule the World’ single” (the band covered the Tears For Fears classic on its 2019 self-titled Teal Album), “Nightmare blunt rotation” and “What’s with these homies ruining the world?” (playing off the “What’s with these homies dissing my girl?” lyric from another Blue album classic, “Buddy Holly”).

On X, one user went viral with a post of the image and the joke , “Weezer undergoing some pretty dramatic lineup changes.”

But one Redditor’s comment summed up how many of the band’s fans likely feel about the image: “Right because I want to associate some of the worst people in the world with my favorite band.”

Weezer’s ‘Blue Album’

Courtesy of DGC

The Blue Album arrived via DGC in May 1994 and peaked at No. 16 on the Billboard 200 the following February. Debut single “Undone – The Sweater Song” reached a high of No. 57 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 6 on the Alternative Airplay chart, while subsequent singles from the album, “Buddy Holly” and “Say It Ain’t So,” peaked at Nos. 2 and 7, respectively, on Alternative Airplay.

Weezer appears on the cover of Billboard ‘s current issue, where it discusses its long touring career and enduring influence on new generations of musicians and fans. The band also appeared at Billboard ‘s Live Music Summit earlier in November, where it was recognized as Legend of Live and participated in a conversation with Billboard Co-Chief Content Officer Jason Lipshutz.
